CaseIdentifierFamily.description:
Normalized family/namespace of a case-within-source identifier.

Used by the deterministic comparator to decide whether two identifiers
are safely comparable. Two identifiers with different families (or one
in ``UNKNOWN``) are *not* treated as comparable; their mismatch never
becomes evidence of different individuals.
CaseIdentifierFamily.title: CaseIdentifierFamily

EvidenceSpan.description: Short verbatim snippet supporting one extracted field.

field.description: Name of the NarrativeSourceCase field this snippet supports.
field.title: Field

quote.description: Short verbatim snippet copied from the narrative.
quote.title: Quote

EvidenceSpan.title: EvidenceSpan

NarrativeSourceCase.description:
Structured source / case signals extracted from one report narrative.

All fields are optional by design: the extractor is precision-oriented
and leaves fields null when the narrative does not provide clear
support. Deterministic normalization (DOI form, family mapping, value
canonicalization) is applied after LLM parsing so downstream
comparison can rely on ``source_identifier`` and
``case_identifier_value_normalized`` without re-normalizing.

multi_patient_source.description: Whether the narrative indicates the source describes multiple patients or cases. Null when unclear.
multi_patient_source.title: Multi Patient Source

single_patient_source.description: Whether the narrative indicates the source describes a single patient or case. Intentionally *not* the negation of multi_patient_source: both may be null when evidence is weak.
single_patient_source.title: Single Patient Source

source_identifier.description: Stable identifier of the underlying source, when present. For literature this should be a DOI (normalized to lowercase, without protocol prefix). For summary-case-like contexts it may be a 'Linked case: ...' string that appears identically across sibling reports.
source_identifier.title: Source Identifier

case_identifier_within_source.description: Surface form of a label for the patient or case *inside* a multi-patient source (e.g. 'Case 2', 'Patient B', 'Subject-01'). Do not confuse with report-specific IDs.
case_identifier_within_source.title: Case Identifier Within Source

case_identifier_type.description: Free-form label from the model, e.g. 'case', 'patient_letter'.
case_identifier_type.title: Case Identifier Type

case_identifier_value_normalized.description: Normalized comparable value within the identifier family, e.g. 'Case 2' -> '2', 'Patient B' -> 'B', 'Subject-01' -> '1'.
case_identifier_value_normalized.title: Case Identifier Value Normalized

likely_report_specific_identifiers.description: Identifier-like strings that more likely identify *this* report than the shared source or a case-within-source (e.g. 'Other Identification Number 48392'). Kept for transparency; never used as a source_identifier.
likely_report_specific_identifiers.title: Likely Report Specific Identifiers

evidence.description: Short verbatim snippets supporting non-null fields.
evidence.title: Evidence

notes.description: Brief free-text explanation for human review.
notes.title: Notes

NarrativeSourceCase.title: NarrativeSourceCase

SourceIdentifierType.description:
Kind of identifier that would link sibling reports to the same source.

``linked_case`` covers strings like ``"Linked case: AB-123456789"`` that
are expected to appear verbatim across reports sharing the same
underlying case. It is classified here as a *source* identifier, not a
*case-within-source* identifier, because its defining property is that
sibling reports carry the identical string.
SourceIdentifierType.title: SourceIdentifierType

SourceType.description: Kind of underlying source the narrative appears to describe.
SourceType.title: SourceType

description:
Precomputed per-report narrative source/case extractions.

Produced once by the secure repo (one LLM call per unique report)
and serialized as a single JSON artifact. Passed to
``PipelineRunner`` to skip live LLM calls during offline
evaluation.

Partial bundles are allowed: ``report_id`` keys present in the
bundle are served from it; missing ``report_id`` keys fall back to
live extraction (or ``None`` if no LLM client is configured on the
runner). This is intentionally more lenient than
``FrozenStatsProvider`` because source/case is advisory — only the
shared-source override path in the decision logic consumes it, and
the override is designed to be skippable.

Attributes
----------
extractions : dict[str, NarrativeSourceCase]
    Mapping of ``report_id`` → per-report extraction.
title: FrozenSourceCaseExtractions
